links.title: Soperator dashboards
links.tooltip: Open related cluster and worker dashboards

panels.title: Reconciles / min
panels.description: Reconcile loop executions per minute summed over the selected controllers, every result included. Scope: the selected physical cluster, component and controller. Rebooter pods are summed across nodes.

targets.expr: 60 * sum(rate(controller_runtime_reconcile_total{cluster=~"$cluster", component=~"$component", component!="", controller=~"$controller"}[$__rate_interval]))

panels.title: Reconcile errors / min
panels.description: Reconciles per minute that returned an error, summed over the selected controllers. Controllers that log failures and return nil (for example rollingupdate) do not count here. Scope: the selected physical cluster, component and controller. Rebooter pods are summed across nodes.

targets.expr: 60 * sum(rate(controller_runtime_reconcile_errors_total{cluster=~"$cluster", component=~"$component", component!="", controller=~"$controller"}[$__rate_interval]))

panels.title: Panics in range
panels.description: Reconcile panics recovered by controller-runtime over the dashboard time range. Any value above zero needs operator logs. Scope: the selected physical cluster, component and controller. Rebooter pods are summed across nodes.

targets.expr: sum(increase(controller_runtime_reconcile_panics_total{cluster=~"$cluster", component=~"$component", component!="", controller=~"$controller"}[$__range]))

panels.title: Terminal errors in range
panels.description: Reconciles that returned a terminal error over the dashboard time range. Terminal errors are not retried by the workqueue. Scope: the selected physical cluster, component and controller. Rebooter pods are summed across nodes.

targets.expr: sum(increase(controller_runtime_terminal_reconcile_errors_total{cluster=~"$cluster", component=~"$component", component!="", controller=~"$controller"}[$__range]))

panels.title: Reconcile timeouts in range
panels.description: Reconciles cancelled by the controller reconciliation timeout over the dashboard time range. Scope: the selected physical cluster, component and controller. Rebooter pods are summed across nodes.

targets.expr: sum(increase(controller_runtime_reconcile_timeouts_total{cluster=~"$cluster", component=~"$component", component!="", controller=~"$controller"}[$__range]))

panels.title: Max workqueue depth
panels.description: Largest current workqueue backlog among the selected controllers. A depth that stays above zero means reconciles cannot keep up with events. Scope: the selected physical cluster, component and controller. Rebooter pods are summed across nodes.

targets.expr: max(workqueue_depth{cluster=~"$cluster", component=~"$component", component!="", name=~"$controller"})

panels.title: Leader election
panels.description: leader_election_master_status per controller process pod: 1 is the active leader, 0 is standby. Processes without leader election have no series. Rebooter pods are excluded because this panel is per pod.

targets.expr: max by (cluster, component, namespace, pod) (leader_election_master_status{cluster=~"$cluster", component=~"$component", component!~"rebooter|"})

panels.title: Scraped controller processes
panels.description: Number of pods currently exposing controller-runtime metrics per component. Rebooter pods equal the number of nodes running the DaemonSet. Zero or a missing component means its ServiceMonitor is not being scraped.

targets.expr: count by (cluster, component, namespace) (count by (cluster, component, namespace, pod) (controller_runtime_max_concurrent_reconciles{cluster=~"$cluster", component=~"$component", component!=""}))

panels.title: Reconciles / min by result
panels.description: Reconcile executions per minute per controller and outcome. success ends without requeue, requeue and requeue_after are explicit requeues, error is a returned error (retried with backoff). Stacked per series.

targets.expr: 60 * sum by (cluster, component, namespace, controller, result) (rate(controller_runtime_reconcile_total{cluster=~"$cluster", component=~"$component", component!="", controller=~"$controller"}[$__rate_interval]))

panels.title: Reconcile errors / min
panels.description: Reconciles per minute that returned an error, per controller. Compare with the result breakdown to see whether errors dominate a controller's loop.

targets.expr: 60 * sum by (cluster, component, namespace, controller) (rate(controller_runtime_reconcile_errors_total{cluster=~"$cluster", component=~"$component", component!="", controller=~"$controller"}[$__rate_interval]))

panels.title: Reconcile duration · p50
panels.description: Median wall time of one reconcile per controller, from controller_runtime_reconcile_time_seconds.

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.5, sum by (cluster, component, namespace, controller, le) (rate(controller_runtime_reconcile_time_seconds_bucket{cluster=~"$cluster", component=~"$component", component!="", controller=~"$controller"}[$__rate_interval])))

panels.title: Reconcile duration · p95
panels.description: 95th percentile wall time of one reconcile per controller. Growth here usually means slow Kube API or Slurm REST calls inside the loop.

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (cluster, component, namespace, controller, le) (rate(controller_runtime_reconcile_time_seconds_bucket{cluster=~"$cluster", component=~"$component", component!="", controller=~"$controller"}[$__rate_interval])))

panels.title: Reconcile duration · p99
panels.description: 99th percentile wall time of one reconcile per controller.

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (cluster, component, namespace, controller, le) (rate(controller_runtime_reconcile_time_seconds_bucket{cluster=~"$cluster", component=~"$component", component!="", controller=~"$controller"}[$__rate_interval])))

panels.title: Active workers
panels.description: Reconcile goroutines currently running per controller (controller_runtime_active_workers).

targets.expr: max by (cluster, component, namespace, controller) (controller_runtime_active_workers{cluster=~"$cluster", component=~"$component", component!="", controller=~"$controller"})

panels.title: Worker saturation
panels.description: Active workers divided by the configured max concurrent reconciles. Sustained values near 100% mean the controller is concurrency-bound and events queue up.

targets.expr: max by (cluster, component, namespace, controller) (controller_runtime_active_workers{cluster=~"$cluster", component=~"$component", component!="", controller=~"$controller"}) / max by (cluster, component, namespace, controller) (controller_runtime_max_concurrent_reconciles{cluster=~"$cluster", component=~"$component", component!="", controller=~"$controller"})

panels.title: Workqueue depth
panels.description: Items waiting in each controller's workqueue. Workqueue metrics carry the controller name in the name label.

targets.expr: max by (cluster, component, namespace, name) (workqueue_depth{cluster=~"$cluster", component=~"$component", component!="", name=~"$controller"})

panels.title: Workqueue adds / min
panels.description: Items enqueued per minute per controller: watch events after predicates plus requeues. This is the event pressure each controller receives.

targets.expr: 60 * sum by (cluster, component, namespace, name) (rate(workqueue_adds_total{cluster=~"$cluster", component=~"$component", component!="", name=~"$controller"}[$__rate_interval]))

panels.title: Workqueue retries / min
panels.description: Items re-added with rate-limited backoff per minute, per controller. Retries follow reconcile errors and explicit requeues without a delay.

targets.expr: 60 * sum by (cluster, component, namespace, name) (rate(workqueue_retries_total{cluster=~"$cluster", component=~"$component", component!="", name=~"$controller"}[$__rate_interval]))

panels.title: Queue latency · p95
panels.description: 95th percentile time an item waits in the workqueue before a worker picks it up.

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (cluster, component, namespace, name, le) (rate(workqueue_queue_duration_seconds_bucket{cluster=~"$cluster", component=~"$component", component!="", name=~"$controller"}[$__rate_interval])))

panels.title: Work duration · p95
panels.description: 95th percentile time a worker spends processing one item, as measured by the workqueue.

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (cluster, component, namespace, name, le) (rate(workqueue_work_duration_seconds_bucket{cluster=~"$cluster", component=~"$component", component!="", name=~"$controller"}[$__rate_interval])))

panels.title: Longest running processor
panels.description: Age of the longest currently running item per controller. A steadily growing line is a stuck reconcile.

targets.expr: max by (cluster, component, namespace, name) (workqueue_longest_running_processor_seconds{cluster=~"$cluster", component=~"$component", component!="", name=~"$controller"})

panels.title: Unfinished work
panels.description: Total seconds of in-progress work per controller that has not finished yet. Large values with few active workers point at long-running reconciles.

targets.expr: max by (cluster, component, namespace, name) (workqueue_unfinished_work_seconds{cluster=~"$cluster", component=~"$component", component!="", name=~"$controller"})

panels.title: Scraped rebooter pods
panels.description: Rebooter DaemonSet pods exposing metrics, one per node running the NodeConfigurator DaemonSet. The rows above sum rebooter pods into one series; this row breaks them down per pod.

targets.expr: count by (cluster) (count by (cluster, pod) (controller_runtime_max_concurrent_reconciles{cluster=~"$cluster", component=~"$component", component="rebooter"}))

panels.title: Top 10 rebooter pods by errors / min
panels.description: Rebooter pods with the highest reconcile error rate. Use the pod name to find the node.

targets.expr: topk(10, 60 * sum by (cluster, pod) (rate(controller_runtime_reconcile_errors_total{cluster=~"$cluster", component=~"$component", component="rebooter"}[$__rate_interval])))

panels.title: Top 10 rebooter pods by reconcile duration · p95
panels.description: Rebooter pods with the slowest reconciles.

targets.expr: topk(10, histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (cluster, pod, le) (rate(controller_runtime_reconcile_time_seconds_bucket{cluster=~"$cluster", component=~"$component", component="rebooter"}[$__rate_interval]))))

panels.title: CPU
panels.description: CPU cores used by each controller process, from process_cpu_seconds_total. Rebooter pods are excluded because this row is per pod and would scale with node count.

targets.expr: sum by (cluster, component, namespace, pod) (rate(process_cpu_seconds_total{cluster=~"$cluster", component=~"$component", component!~"rebooter|"}[$__rate_interval]))

panels.title: Resident memory
panels.description: Resident set size of each controller process.

targets.expr: max by (cluster, component, namespace, pod) (process_resident_memory_bytes{cluster=~"$cluster", component=~"$component", component!~"rebooter|"})

panels.title: Goroutines
panels.description: Live goroutines per controller process. A monotonic climb is a leak, often from unbounded requeues or watches.

targets.expr: max by (cluster, component, namespace, pod) (go_goroutines{cluster=~"$cluster", component=~"$component", component!~"rebooter|"})

panels.title: Controllers and how to read this dashboard

options.content:
All panels come from the metrics that controller-runtime registers for every manager: `controller_runtime_*` for the reconcile loop, `workqueue_*` for its queue, `leader_election_master_status`, and the Go and process collectors. No soperator-specific metric code is involved.

**Component and controller labels**

`component` is a static target label set by each ServiceMonitor (`soperator`, `soperatorchecks`, `sconfigcontroller`, `rebooter`). It survives the o11y remote-write, unlike `job`, and separates processes that register a controller with the same name. `controller` is the controller-runtime name passed to `Named()`; workqueue metrics carry the same value in the `name` label. `namespace` is the namespace of the metrics pod, which separates several sconfigcontroller instances.

| Component | Controller | Reconciles |
| --- | --- | --- |
| soperator | cluster | SlurmCluster CR: renders and applies every Slurm component. |
| soperator | nodeset | NodeSet CR: worker StatefulSets, power state and node-local config. |
| soperator | nodeconfigurator | NodeConfigurator CR: per-node DaemonSets (rebooter, sysctl, custom containers). |
| soperator | rollingupdate | Worker StatefulSet rollouts with Slurm drain and handoff. See Soperator / Rollouts. |
| soperator | nodetopology | Kubernetes Node topology labels into the cluster topology ResourceDistribution. |
| soperator | workertopology | SlurmCluster topology settings into topology.conf. |
| soperator, soperatorchecks | soperatorchecks.slurmapiclients | Keeps a Slurm REST client per SlurmCluster for the other controllers in the process. |
| soperatorchecks | soperatorchecks.activecheck | ActiveCheck CR: CronJobs and Jobs that run health checks. |
| soperatorchecks | soperatorchecks.activecheckjob | Finished check Jobs: results into Slurm node state and conditions. |
| soperatorchecks | soperatorchecks.slurmnodes | Slurm node drain reasons into Kubernetes Node conditions; undrains nodes whose compute instance was replaced. |
| soperatorchecks | soperatorchecks.k8snodes | Kubernetes Node drain and reboot conditions: drains the Slurm node and requests reboots. |
| soperatorchecks | soperatorchecks.serviceaccount | ServiceAccount and RBAC used by check Jobs. |
| soperatorchecks | soperatorchecks.podephemeralstorage | Worker pod ephemeral storage usage checks. |
| sconfigcontroller | jailedconfig | JailedConfig CR: files inside the jail and Slurm reconfigure. |
| rebooter | rebooter | One per node: reboots the node when requested by soperator. |

**Reading the panels**

- `result=success` is a reconcile that returned without requeue, `requeue` and `requeue_after` are explicit requeues, `error` is a returned error that the workqueue retries with backoff.
- A controller can fail without incrementing errors: rollingupdate logs operational failures and returns nil to keep its polling interval, so use Soperator / Rollouts for rollout health.
- Workqueue depth above zero for long periods, or worker saturation near 100%, means the controller cannot keep up with events. Check reconcile duration first, then Kube API and Slurm REST latency.
- Rebooter runs one pod per node. Controller rows sum or max its pods into one series; the per-pod panels (Leader election, Process) exclude it, and the Rebooter row shows per-pod detail. Series without a `component` label (other controller-runtime operators in the cluster, such as the VictoriaMetrics operator) are excluded everywhere.
- Missing series mean the component is not scraped: check the ServiceMonitor, its metrics Service endpoints and vmagent targets.

**Scope:** `$cluster` is the physical cluster label added by remote-write; a local datasource without the label uses All. For manual imports `var-datasource=<UID>` selects another datasource.

list.description: Infrastructure cluster from the optional external cluster label, distinct from a SlurmCluster CR. O11y can set this hidden variable; a local datasource without the label uses All. For manual scope selection, set var-cluster in the dashboard URL.
